 Korea Open: Shida Begins Afresh
 Tuesday, November 3, 2026
 TEXT BY DIANNE PIERRE | JNANESH SALIAN/BADMINTONPHOTO 
 SHARE 
 Chiharu Shida ‘s badminton book has a new chapter.
 At YEOSU VICTOR Korea Open 2026 on Tuesday, Shida and new partner Ririna Hiramoto booked their place in the second round with a 21-18 21-11 win over Chen Su Yu/Chen Han.
 The pair had only recently made their debut at the French Open and arrived in Yeosu still searching for rhythm after a hectic spell away from the international circuit.
 “After France, we had about a week before domestic competitions and there wasn’t much time to train together,” Shida said. “When we arrived here, it almost felt like we were practicing together for the first time. That lack of practice showed a little at the beginning but our combination gradually improved.”
 For Shida, a former world No.1 who returned to competition this season after a break from the tour, the partnership represents both a fresh challenge and a chance to pass on her experience to the younger generation.
 Hiramoto admitted she was initially intimidated by the prospect of partnering one of Japan’s biggest names.
 “At first I was a little nervous,” she said. “She is older and was also a senior at my former school. I wasn’t sure whether I would be good enough.
 “But Shida is really good at communicating with everyone. She would start conversations and create a relaxed atmosphere and gradually I became less nervous. That positive environment has helped us on court.”
 The 20-year-old has already identified plenty she hopes to learn from her new partner, particularly Shida’s renowned defensive game and court craft. For her part, Shida believes the contrast between the pair could become their greatest strength.
 “I want to embrace the energy and freshness she brings,” Shida said. “The age difference gives us a unique appeal and there are many things we can learn from each other. As long as we make the most of each other’s strengths, we can develop into a good pair.”
 Shida is not the only Olympic medallist starting afresh in Yeosu.
 While the Japanese star won bronze at Paris 2024 alongside Nami Matsuyama, Wang Chang claimed men’s doubles silver with Liang Wei Keng. This week, the recently-crowned world champions find themselves testing new combinations as attention begins turning towards the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
 This week, Wang partners Xie Haonan while Liang teams up with Hu Ke Yuan.
 Wang (left) and Xie during their 21-14 22-24 21-17 win over Bryan Jeremy Goonting/Muhammad Haikal. 
 For Wang and Xie, both from the Zhejiang Province, the tournament marked their first international appearance together. According to Wang, the decision to split the established partnerships was aimed at bringing together different playing styles and ideas, allowing players to learn from one another and compensate for each other’s weaknesses.
 “Our goal is still to win titles. Our biggest target is simply to give our best in every round,” Wang said.
